reason: The main HuggingGPT demo needs OpenAI/HF keys, but the README's TaskBench 'Construct Your Own Tool Graph' step (generate_graph.py) runs offline on CPU with bundled data.
demo: taskbench/README.md 'Setup' + 'Construct Your Own Tool Graph': python generate_graph.py --tool_desc <tool library> --dependency_type resource|temporal, then python visualize_graph.py --data_dir <dir>
goal: Set up the TaskBench environment the way taskbench/README.md 'Setup' describes (a Python 3.8 environment with taskbench/requirements.txt installed). From /work/JARVIS/taskbench, `python generate_graph.py --tool_desc <tool_desc.json> --dependency_type resource` must turn a bundled tool library such as data_huggingface/tool_desc.json into a tool graph JSON with nodes and links, `--dependency_type temporal` must do the same for the API-style library data_dailylifeapis/tool_desc.json, and `python visualize_graph.py --data_dir <dir>` must render <dir>/graph_desc.json to a PDF.
check: The hidden test builds resource graphs for two bundled tool libraries and a temporal graph for the API library on copies of the data, checks their nodes and links, and renders one graph to a PDF with visualize_graph.py.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Goal leaks an install hint: '(it needs the click package; install what else the script imports)'. taskbench/README.md:129-134 says to `pip install -r requirements.txt` in a Python 3.8 env; the goal tells the agent the test only needs click.

Goal also hands over a gotcha the README does not state ('Work on a copy ... because the script writes its output next to the input file name'); the oracle copies the data itself, so the hint is unnecessary.

Coverage too narrow: the oracle only runs generate_graph.py --dependency_type resource, which imports nothing but json and click (generate_graph.py:1-2), so an install of click alone passes. The README's temporal graph (README.md:227) and the visualize_graph.py check it names (README.md:236; networkx/matplotlib/scipy from requirements.txt) are untested.
Minor dead code in v1: `for f in ["tool_desc.json", "tool_desc.json".replace("tools","graph")]` loads the same file twice.
